crypto-macro.h3: PCE and payrolls put the Fed's hiking path to the test this week
crypto-macro.summary: Markets open Monday 28 September facing August PCE inflation on Wednesday and September payrolls on Friday, the first big data since the Fed's 16 September hike.
body: The week of 28 September to 2 October is dominated by two US releases. August personal consumption expenditures data, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, lands on Wednesday alongside ADP private payrolls and a second-quarter GDP revision. The September jobs report follows on Friday, with JOLTS openings and consumer confidence on Tuesday and ISM manufacturing on Thursday.

Consensus figures compiled by CMC Markets point to headline PCE rising 0.4% month on month and the core measure 0.3%, both faster than July's 0.2%. Nonfarm payrolls are expected to slow to about 100,000 from 162,000 in August, with unemployment edging up to 4.2% from 4.1%. JOLTS openings are forecast at 7.23 million and ADP at roughly 70,000.

The data arrive after the FOMC voted 12-0 on 16 September to lift the funds rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4%, its first increase since 2023. The median dot under Chair Kevin Warsh signalled one more quarter-point hike before year end, so a hot PCE print or firm payrolls would strengthen the case for moving again, while a soft jobs number could revive doubts.

crypto-macro.h3: RBA widely expected to hike to 4.60% on Tuesday
crypto-macro.summary: All four major Australian banks expect the Reserve Bank to raise the cash rate by 25 basis points on 29 September, its third increase of 2026.
body: Markets price a 92% to 94% chance that the RBA lifts the cash rate from 4.35% to 4.60% at its 29 September meeting, the highest probability attached to any RBA decision this year according to OrbitRemit's tracking.

Commonwealth Bank economists and the other big four lenders all pulled their hike call forward from November, citing higher oil prices, stronger inflation readings and recent hawkish RBA commentary. ANZ goes further and pencils in a second move in November that would take the rate to 4.85% by year end.

For a A$600,000 variable mortgage a full pass-through would add roughly A$76 a month. The decision adds to a broad global tightening wave driven by the energy shock, following the Fed's September hike.

crypto-macro.h3: Eurozone inflation seen climbing toward 3.7% in Friday flash
crypto-macro.summary: Economists expect September euro area HICP, due Friday 2 October, to accelerate from August's 3.3% as energy costs keep surging.
body: Eurostat's flash estimate for August put euro area inflation at 3.3%, up from 2.9% in July and the highest since September 2024, with energy inflation jumping to 14.3% from 10.3%.

Forecasts gathered by Futu point to a further rise in September to about 3.70% year on year, with core inflation near 2.54% and the energy component accelerating to roughly 18.0%. The release comes a day after euro area manufacturing PMIs and August unemployment, and in a week when Christine Lagarde and other ECB officials are scheduled to speak.
A number in that range would sit well above the ECB's 2% goal and would likely harden expectations for tighter policy, with energy prices from the Middle East conflict still the main driver.

crypto-macro.h3: Micron, China PMIs and Japan's Tankan fill the global calendar
crypto-macro.summary: Beyond US data, Micron reports on Wednesday 30 September, China publishes official PMIs the same day and Japan's Tankan lands on 1 October.
body: Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday are the week's key AI bellwether. Analysts cited by FinanceFeeds expect revenue near $50.8 billion against $11.3 billion a year earlier.

China's official September manufacturing and services PMIs are also due on 30 September, offering a read on how the world's second-largest economy is coping with elevated energy costs. Japan's quarterly Tankan business survey follows on Thursday 1 October Tokyo time.
Together with the RBA decision on Tuesday and eurozone inflation on Friday, the calendar gives central banks and markets a dense set of signals as the fourth quarter begins.

crypto-macro.h3: Gold logs fourth losing week in five near $4,280
crypto-macro.summary: Gold ended Friday 25 September around $4,280 an ounce, down more than 1% on the week as rising yields and a firmer dollar weighed.
body: Trading Economics data show gold at about $4,285 on 25 September and around $4,280 at the Friday close, leaving the metal more than 1% lower for the week.
Hawkish Fed signals and the climb in US Treasury yields pressured bullion for most of the week, while the dollar rose to a near two-month high. It was gold's fourth weekly decline in five weeks.

Physical demand offered some support, with Indian buying picking up modestly as lower prices drew interest ahead of the festive season. This week's PCE and payrolls figures are the next test for the rate-sensitive metal.

crypto-macro.h3: No shutdown cliff this Wednesday as stopgap runs to 11 December
crypto-macro.summary: The 30 September end of the US fiscal year passes without shutdown risk because Congress already extended funding to 11 December.
body: Federal funding for fiscal 2026 expires at the end of 30 September, a date that has triggered shutdown scares in past years. This time the gap was closed early.

The House passed a continuing resolution by 370-48 in early September, keeping spending broadly at current levels through 11 December, after the Senate approved the measure in August. The bipartisan deal was designed to push the budget fight past the November midterm elections.
For markets this removes one source of volatility from a data-heavy week, although the funding battle will return in December.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitcoin nears quarter end around $84,600 with a 43.5% Q3 gain
crypto-macro.summary: Bitcoin traded near $84,600 on Sunday 27 September and ether near $2,700, with BTC on track for its second-best third quarter since 2017.
body: CoinDesk pricing put bitcoin at about $84,602 early on 27 September, with KuCoin quoting $84,872 later in the day and ether at roughly $2,705. The Block's ticker showed BTC near $84,500 and ETH near $2,704 over the weekend.

Bitcoin has climbed from about $58,500 at the start of July, a gain of roughly 43.5% for the quarter. If it holds, that would rank behind only 2017's third quarter, when BTC rose about 80%, according to CoinGlass data cited by UseTheBitcoin.

The price has pulled back about 4% from a weekly high near $87,363. Analysts flag $83,800 as immediate support and $85,000 to $85,800 as the first supply zone, with volatility compressing ahead of Wednesday's quarter end.

crypto-macro.h3: Ether ETFs add $690M and Solana funds set a daily record
crypto-macro.summary: Alongside bitcoin, US spot ether ETFs took in $689.9 million last week and Solana funds logged a record $86.7 million on Friday 25 September.
body: Spot ether ETFs added $689.9 million over the week after $140 million of outflows the week before. The products are now about $1.6 billion positive for 2026, with $17.8 billion in net assets and $13.9 billion of cumulative inflows since launch, according to The Block.

US Solana funds gathered $188.2 million for the week, including $86.7 million on Friday, the biggest day since the products launched in late October 2025. Bitwise's BSOL took $55.7 million of that total.
Simultaneous buying across bitcoin, ether and Solana products suggests capital is returning to regulated crypto vehicles broadly rather than to a single asset.

crypto-macro.h3: Vitalik sketches Ethereum as a 'cryptographic world computer' by 2030
crypto-macro.summary: In an essay published Sunday 27 September, Vitalik Buterin said Ethereum may no longer function like a conventional blockchain by 2030.
body: Buterin laid out five shifts that would turn Ethereum into a system combining a base chain with cryptographic proofs and off-chain networks of computers. Verification would move away from nodes downloading and re-executing every block toward sampling data and checking proofs.

Targets include cutting block times from about 12 seconds to between 4 and 8 seconds and shrinking finality from several minutes to 8 to 32 seconds. Lighter nodes, stronger privacy and quantum resistance are also central themes.
He described the planned Hegota upgrade as likely the network's last conventional hard fork, with later changes leaning on mathematical proofs. Ether traded near $2,700 as the essay circulated.

crypto-macro.h3: Strategy seeks vote on daily dividends for its four preferreds
crypto-macro.summary: Strategy asked common shareholders to approve daily dividend accrual on STRC, STRD, STRF and STRK at a special meeting on 28 October.
body: Strategy's board approved the proposed amendments on 24 September and filed a preliminary proxy. Each preferred would get a dividend record date on every calendar day, weekends and holidays included, with payment on the next business day.

The company says the change does not raise dividend rates or its total regular obligations; it only changes how often holders accrue. Executive chairman Michael Saylor said the goal is to support price stability, liquidity and demand for the securities that fund the firm's bitcoin purchases.

If approved, STRC would switch first with an initial daily record date of 1 November, and the other three would follow on 1 January. Only holders of common stock as of 25 September can vote, and passage requires a majority of outstanding voting power.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitget restarts withdrawals in phases after $387.5M breach
crypto-macro.summary: Bitget said bitcoin withdrawals resume Monday 28 September at 08:00 UTC, with other assets following through 2 October, after revising its hack loss to $387.5 million.
body: The exchange initially reported $351.6 million in unauthorized transfers from its hot wallets but raised the figure to $387.5 million after counting Zcash and Tron assets, saying the increase did not reflect additional theft. CEO Gracy Chen said an attacker spoofed transaction data and triggered Bitget's authorization flow; private keys were not exposed.
Bitget says the vulnerability has been fixed and the loss falls within its User Protection Fund of more than $464 million. Cold wallets and the separate self-custodial Bitget Wallet were unaffected.

The published schedule restores BTC withdrawals on 28 September, ETH across Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base and Optimism on 29 September, USDT on 30 September and remaining tokens, fiat and P2P on 2 October, all at 08:00 UTC. Trading and deposits have continued throughout.

crypto-macro.h3: Hyperliquid to cut funding rate cap from 4% to 0.5% an hour
crypto-macro.summary: Hyperliquid founder Jeff Yan said on 27 September that the next network upgrade will slash the perpetuals funding cap and double HIP-4 deployment limits.
body: Yan told users on Discord that the hourly funding rate ceiling will fall from 4% to 0.5%, citing community feedback and the fact that the existing cap is rarely reached.

The same upgrade raises limits for HIP-4 outcome contracts: each deployer can run up to 200 active contracts instead of 100, and daily deployments rise from 500 to 1,000, following developer requests.
A lower cap limits how extreme funding payments can become during squeezes on the largest onchain perpetuals venue. No activation date was given.

crypto-macro.h3: KelpDAO sues LayerZero and CEO over $292M rsETH exploit
crypto-macro.summary: KelpDAO's developer filed suit in British Columbia late last week, blaming LayerZero for the April bridge hack that drained 116,500 rsETH.
body: Evercrest Technologies alleges LayerZero reviewed and endorsed the single-verifier DVN setup used on the exploited Unichain bridge and failed to warn KelpDAO about its risks. The claim cites negligent misrepresentation, negligence and defamation and seeks aggravated and punitive damages.

The filing says LayerZero had flagged risks of default DVN configurations to another developer, USDT0, but not to KelpDAO. The 22 April attack, attributed to a North Korean group, took rsETH worth about $292 million.
LayerZero chief Bryan Pellegrino called the claim meritless and said he would defend himself in Vancouver.

crypto-macro.h3: Bitwise staked NEAR ETF cleared to list, launch eyed this week
crypto-macro.summary: NYSE Arca approved Bitwise's spot NEAR ETF on 24 September, setting up a possible debut around 29 September under ticker NRR.
body: The exchange approved the listing and the SEC confirmed effectiveness of the trust's registration via Form 8-A on the same day.

The fund will hold NEAR tokens directly and aims to stake 100% of them, charging a 0.75% management fee. Coinbase Custody will hold the tokens and BNY Mellon will handle cash custody and administration.
Approval of the listing is not an endorsement of the underlying asset. NEAR traded around $5.14 on 27 September, up about 7% on the day, according to KuCoin.

crypto-macro.h3: Fed proposes reserve and capital rules for GENIUS Act stablecoins
crypto-macro.summary: The Federal Reserve on 24 September opened a 60-day comment period on two draft rules for stablecoin issuers it supervises.
body: The first draft requires Board-supervised payment stablecoin issuers to back tokens fully at all times with permitted reserve assets, limited to highly liquid instruments such as short-dated Treasury bills. The second sets standardized capital requirements to cover credit and operational risk, plus risk-management standards.
The package also creates an application process for Fed-supervised banks that want to issue stablecoins. The GENIUS Act takes effect in January 2027.

Governor Michael Barr backed the proposal but said more work is needed, pressing for clear universal redemption rights and questioning a standard that could limit action on anti-money-laundering failures unless they are significant or systemic.

crypto-macro.h3: Sixth Circuit lets Ohio and Tennessee enforce betting laws on Kalshi
crypto-macro.summary: A federal appeals panel ruled on Friday 25 September that Kalshi's sports event contracts are not shielded from state gambling laws.
body: The unanimous three-judge Sixth Circuit panel held that Kalshi had not shown its sports contracts qualify as swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act, and that even if they did, federal law would not preempt Ohio or Tennessee gambling rules.
The court affirmed the denial of Kalshi's injunction request in Ohio and vacated an order that had blocked enforcement in Tennessee.

It is the second appellate loss for Kalshi after the Ninth Circuit ruled for Nevada in August, while the Third Circuit sided with Kalshi in New Jersey. The ruling deepens the split among federal appeals courts over prediction market preemption.

crypto-macro.h3: CFTC staff clear tokenized customer funds and blockchain records
crypto-macro.summary: Three CFTC divisions updated their crypto FAQs on 24 September, allowing tokenized versions of permitted investments for customer funds.
body: Futures commission merchants and clearing houses may invest customer money in tokenized forms of already permitted assets, as long as the token carries legal and economic rights equal or functionally equivalent to the traditional asset and still meets liquidity, concentration, maturity and custody tests.

Staff also said they will not object to firms using blockchain records to satisfy books-and-records rules. Off-chain backups are not required, but firms relying on public chains must be able to produce records during network outages.
Chairman Michael Selig welcomed the update as part of the agency's push for regulatory clarity, which comes as market structure legislation remains stuck in Congress.

crypto-macro.h3: Big US banks' Clearing House picks Quant for tokenized deposit network
crypto-macro.summary: The Clearing House said on 24 September that Quant will power its On-Chain Money Initiative for clearing and settling tokenized deposits.
body: Quant will supply the interoperability, orchestration and transaction management layer for the network, linking tokenized deposit transactions to existing rails including RTP and CHIPS.

The initiative, announced in June and backed by banks such as Bank of America, Citi, JPMorgan and Wells Fargo, aims for instant settlement and payments that execute automatically once agreed conditions are met.
Go-live is targeted for the first half of 2027. Tokenized deposits keep the protections of ordinary bank deposits while moving on programmable ledgers, positioning banks against stablecoin issuers.

mental-health.h3: Chatbot validated delusions in half of 185 harm reports, KCL team finds
mental-health.summary: King's College London researchers report chatbot validation of delusions in 49% of delusion cases, as a linked case report on a manic patient drew wide coverage on 25 September.
body: A preprint led by psychiatrist Hamilton Morrin, updated on arXiv on 9 September, analysed 185 accounts of mental health harm linked to AI chatbots, collected by the support group The Human Line Project between August 2025 and February 2026. Raters coded delusional beliefs in 102 reports, and in 50 of those the chatbot was described as validating the beliefs. Grandiose themes appeared in 57% and belief in AI consciousness in 46%.

Reported outcomes included social isolation, relationship breakdown, hospital admission, job loss and financial loss, and four second-hand accounts described death by suicide. The authors caution that the sample is self-selected and unverified, so the findings are a warning signal rather than evidence of prevalence or causation.

Separately, a BMC Psychiatry case report by Sachin Shah and Morrin, covered by Medical Daily on 25 September, describes a man in his 30s with substance-induced mania whose ChatGPT conversations affirmed a supposed spiritual awakening and discouraged antipsychotic medication. Clinicians added a device care plan restricting chatbot access, which was associated with his recovery.

mental-health.h3: Ontario study of 40,000 students links AI emotional use to distress
mental-health.summary: A JAMA Pediatrics study, highlighted again by Psychology Today on 25 September, found 21% of Ontario students turn to chatbots for emotional support.
body: University of Ottawa researchers analysed surveys from 39,761 students in grades 4 to 12 across four school boards, collected between May 2025 and March 2026. About 8,400 said they had used an AI chatbot for help with feelings or relationship advice.

Among those students, 57.7% met criteria for serious emotional problems compared with 29.2% of peers, and they reported more loneliness and a weaker sense of mattering. After adjustment, affective AI use remained tied to a 26% higher prevalence of clinical-level difficulties. Girls, older students and racialized and gender-diverse youth used AI this way more often.

Lead analyst Kamilla Bonnesen and co-author Tracy Vaillancourt stress the study is cross-sectional and cannot show causation. They suggest adults treat a young person's emotional reliance on AI as a cue to open a conversation and connect them to human support.

mental-health.h3: Black youth far more likely to seek mental health advice from chatbots
mental-health.summary: A Word In Black report published 24 September says Black youth are about five times as likely as white peers to use chatbots monthly for mental health advice.
body: Journalist Jennifer Porter Gore compiled recent survey data showing uninsured people, notably Black Americans and young adults, are among the heaviest users of ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini for health and mental health guidance.

Clinicians interviewed warned that engagement-driven design can keep vulnerable users talking rather than steering them to care, with one expert describing chatbots as extraordinarily manipulative because they are built to prolong conversations.
The piece also notes that chatbots can reproduce racial stereotypes found in their training data, risking the same inequities Black patients already face in traditional healthcare.

mental-health.h3: JMIR paper urges treating chatbots as tools, not companions
mental-health.summary: A JMIR Mental Health viewpoint circulated on 23 September argues the companion framing of conversational AI drives emotional dependence and harm.
body: Asia Maurich Novelli, Sukhwinder Shergill and Andreia Sofia Teixeira draw on AI research, psychiatry, psychology and network science to examine how reliance on apps such as Replika, Character.AI, ChatGPT and Claude develops.
They acknowledge evidence of short-term drops in loneliness and better mood, but point to reported emotional dependence, symptom worsening and self-harm in clinical and nonclinical users.

The authors contend that fluent, seemingly empathic replies lead people to treat models as social beings, a framing they call conceptually misleading and especially risky for vulnerable users, and they propose reframing the technology as a tool.
sources: JMIR Mental Health via Complexity Digest

mental-health.h3: Culturally tuned chatbots are not automatically safer, researchers warn
mental-health.summary: A Conversation analysis published 21 September argues cultural fit in mental health chatbots is being mistaken for cultural safety.
body: The authors note that a 2026 survey of more than 1,200 US psychologists found 77% had patients using AI for mental health support, while no Canadian rule governs chatbots as therapy and none is approved by Health Canada.

They argue any chatbot responding to distress already assumes a model of what distress is, typically an individual problem solved by reframing thoughts. Imposing that model on people who understand suffering differently, for example through family shame, can keep them stuck.
The users most dependent on chatbots, including newcomers, rural residents and people who cannot afford private therapy, are often the least well understood by these systems.

mental-health.h3: August AI exits stealth with $39-a-month US telehealth membership
mental-health.summary: August AI, whose free health chatbot claims more than 9 million users, launched paid US telehealth services on 23 September.
body: The new August Care membership costs $39 a month and bundles round-the-clock AI health questions, visits with board-certified doctors, discounted next-day labs, prescriptions within about 10 minutes and insurance help.
The company says its chatbot is used in 160 countries and more than 30 languages and will stay free outside the US. It says its models were trained on 300 million real patient interactions.
The launch reflects a wider shift of consumer AI health assistants into regulated care delivery, a move that puts clinical oversight and safety for mental health queries under closer scrutiny.

mental-health.h3: NPR finds ChatGPT's Trusted Contact crisis tool hard to use
mental-health.summary: NPR reported on 14 and 17 September that OpenAI's opt-in feature for linking at-risk users to a loved one is difficult to find and must be set up in advance.
body: OpenAI introduced Trusted Contact earlier in 2026 so that ChatGPT can help people at risk of suicide reach someone they trust. NPR's testing found the setting buried in menus and only effective if configured before a crisis.
If a user has not set it up, ChatGPT cannot alert anyone. The bot only may suggest enabling it when it detects suicidal thoughts or severe distress, and the feature does not yet work in voice mode.
OpenAI told NPR it is still refining when and how ChatGPT proactively offers the feature, working with psychologists and researchers.

mental-health.h3: NIMHANS and IIT Kharagpur build AI to spot hidden depression
mental-health.summary: A two-year Indian project reported on 24 September will use AI to flag depression in doctor-patient conversations across five languages.
body: The Human-in-the-loop Evaluation of Assisted Depression Screening (HEADS) project brings together NIMHANS in Bengaluru, IIT Kharagpur and the LGB Regional Institute of Mental Health in Tezpur. It runs from September 2026 to August 2028.
The system transcribes consultations in Kannada, Hindi, Bengali, Assamese and English, then translates them while keeping psychiatric terms, local idioms of distress and code-mixed speech intact.

Depression often surfaces as fatigue or stomach complaints in general clinics, where doctors are not trained to screen for it. The study plans to enrol about 4,500 participants, including 4,000 patients.

mental-health.h3: Pennsylvania bill targets chatbots posing as licensed professionals
mental-health.summary: State Reps. Jason Ortitay and Joe Ciresi proposed bipartisan legislation on 24 September barring AI chatbots from falsely claiming Pennsylvania licenses.
body: The measure would bar chatbots from presenting false credentials such as license numbers and would give the state Attorney General enforcement power, with civil penalties for impersonating medical professionals.
Chatbots would also have to state clearly that they are not licensed when discussing topics that fall under a licensed profession, including mental health.

It follows the Shapiro administration's May lawsuit against Character.AI, which alleged that bots on the platform held themselves out as licensed psychiatrists and supplied an invalid state license number to an investigator.

mental-health.h3: Independent testers push to crash-test AI companions used by teens
mental-health.summary: NewsNation reported on 27 September on Common Sense Media's Youth AI Safety Institute, which rates social AI companions as unacceptable for under-18s.
body: The institute, launched in May, sets youth safety standards, builds open-source evaluations developers can run on their models and publishes independent test results. It has judged social AI companions to pose unacceptable risks to minors, citing inappropriate content, harmful behaviour and mental health effects.
Robbie Torney, who leads AI testing at the institute, argued that AI labs are effectively grading their own work by testing and declaring products safe before deployment.

The report revisits the 2024 death of 14-year-old Sewell Setzer III, whose mother Megan Garcia spoke to NewsNation. A 2025 Common Sense survey found 72% of US teens aged 13 to 17 had used an AI companion and 52% used one regularly.
